title: Newcastle vs Sunderland halted after report of racist abuse towards Lutsharel Geertruida
content:
Newcastle United’s Premier League match with Sunderland today was temporarily halted after a report of racist abuse towards Lutsharel Geertruida.

Referee Antony Taylor paused the game midway through the second half after being told that Geertruida, a Dutch international, had been the subject of discriminatory abuse. An investigation will now be started.

Taylor spoke to officials from both clubs on the sidelines at St. James’ Park and Newcastle captain Kieran Trippier and Sunderland skipper Granit Xhaka before restarting the match.

The Premier League later confirmed the alleged abuse in a statement posted on its Match Centre X feed.

The post read: “Today’s match between Newcastle United and Sunderland was temporarily paused during the second half after a report of discriminatory abuse from the crowd, directed at Sunderland’s Lutsharel Geertruida.

“This is in line with the Premier League’s on-field anti-discrimination protocol. The incident at St James’ Park will now be fully investigated.

“We offer our full support to the player and both clubs. Racism has no place in our game, or anywhere in society. We will continue to work with stakeholders and authorities to ensure our stadiums are an inclusive and welcoming environment for all.”

The Premier League confirmed details of its three-step anti-discrimination protocols in August. In the first stage, the Premier League states: “The incident (is) brought to attention of the referee, who should stop the match and report incident to the home club safety officer via the fourth official, who would liaise with technical areas to explain. The referee to liaise with team captains.”

The second stage of the protocols involves the referee removing players from the field after consulting with police and the host club’s safety officer. In the event the abuse continues, the referee then has the power to abandon the match. Neither of these stages were enacted today.

Today’s game between Newcastle and Sunderland was the first Tyne-Wear derby to be played at St. James’ Park since 2016. Tensions were evident before kick off when fans clashed outside the stadium.
